article.title: SaxonC samples
article.p: SaxonC's interfaces are custom-designed interface for all XML processing. The APIs are useful when you want to write your own applications in C/C++, Python or PHP programming languages that invoke Saxon XSLT transforms, XQuery, and evaluate XPath expressions (for more information see Using XSLT, Using XQuery, Evaluating XPath expressions and Using XML Schema (XSD) respectively).

This section of the documentation describes some example code in C/C++, PHP and Python to help get started using SaxonC. A number of samples, test suite drivers (for W3C test suite) written in PHP and Python and unit test code for C/C++ and PHP can be found in the samples directory of the SaxonC installation. Samples and unit tests for Python can be found in the pypi directory.
The SaxonC resources GitHub repository contains all the samples, unit tests and test drivers released in the products for C/C++, Python and PHP.

section.title: C Samples
section.p: The samples/cTests directory in the SaxonC download contains C code samples for running XSLT, XQuery and XPath, along with the build and run scripts. These tests provide various examples of the use of the SaxonC C API. For a step by step guide of building your own C application see Using XSLT from C application, Using XQuery from C and Evaluating XPath expressions from C, respectively

To build SaxonC on C, the following files are required: SaxonCGlue.c, SaxonXProcessor.c and SaxonCXPath.c. Firstly, cd samples/cTests then compile the sample test code by running the build script build64-linux.sh file for linux, build64-mac.sh for MacOS and build64-windows.bat on Windows. section.title: C++ samples
section.p: The samples/cppTests directory in the SaxonC download contains C++ code samples for running XSLT, XQuery, XPath and Schema Validation, along with the build and run scripts. These tests provide various examples of the use of the SaxonC C++ API. The following sections provide a helpful step by step guide to build your own C++ application: Using XSLT from C++, Using XQuery from C++, Evaluating XPath expressions from C++ and Using XML Schema (XSD) from C++, respectively

To build SaxonC on C++, the following files are required: SaxonCGlue.c, SaxonCXPath.c, XdmValue.cpp, XdmItem.cpp, XdmNode.cpp, XdmAtomicValue.cpp, XdmFunctionItem.cpp, XdmArray.cpp, XdmMap.cpp, SaxonProcessor.cpp, Xslt30Processor.cpp, XsltExecutable.cpp, XQueryProcessor.cpp, XPathProcessor.cpp and SchemaValidator.cpp. To compile the samples in C++ execute the build64-[PLATFORM].sh file in the samples/cppTests directory for Linux and Mac OS, or the buildCPPSaxon[EDITION].bat file for Windows. section.title: PHP samples
section.p: The samples/php directory in the SaxonC download contains various samples for XSLT, XQuery, XPath and Schema Validation (namely: xsltExamples.php, xslt30Examples.php, xqueryExamples.php, xpathExamples.php, and validatorExamples.php) and associated files, as well as PHP unit tests for XSLT (xslt30_PHPUnit.php). These files contain many useful examples which will help get you started. The unit tests run under PHPUnit for PHP 7.2 which can be downloaded and installed separately in the same directory as the unit tests.

The following example shows how to debug if something unexpected is happening. It is also very useful to examine the apache error.log file:
section.samp:
<?php
  $xmlfile = "xml/foo.xml";
  $xslFile = "xsl/foo.xsl";
  $proc = new Saxon\SaxonProcessor();
  $xsltProc = $proc->newXslt30Processor();
  $executable = $xsltProc->compileFromFile($xslFile);
  
  $result = $executable->transformFileToString($xmlFile);
  if($result == NULL) {
    if($executable->exceptionOccurred()){
        $errCode = $executable->getErrorCode();
        $errMessage = $executable->getErrorMessage();
        echo 'Expected error: Code='.$errCode.' Message='.$errMessage;
      $xsltProc->exceptionClear();
    }
  }
  echo $result;
  $xsltProc->clearParameters();
  $xsltProc->clearProperties();
?>

section.title: Python samples
section.p: The pypi directory in the SaxonC download includes the unit test files test_saxonc.py and test_saxon_schema.py, which contain a collection of Python unit test cases to be run with the pytest framework. The pyunit tests can be run with the following command:

In the pypi/testsuite_driver directory, you will also find the test driver for running the W3C test suite for XSLT 3.0 against SaxonC. The test suite itself is on GitHub: repository w3c/xslt30-test. The test suite driver can be run as follows:
section.kbd: python3 xslt30_test_suite_driver.py [TEST SUITE DIR] -o [RESULTS OUTPUT DIR]
section.p: The test driver also provides options for running individual test cases or test sets:
To help get started with SaxonC and Python, the pypi/samples directory also includes some python example scripts: saxon_example.py, saxon_example2.py and saxon_example3.py.
Example 1: Python script using the SaxonC-HE API with a simple stylesheet test.xsl:
section.samp:
from saxonche import *
with PySaxonProcessor(license=False) as proc:
print(proc.version) try: xsltproc = proc.new_xslt30_processor() document = proc.parse_xml(xml_text="<out><person>text1</person><person>text2</person><person>text3</person></out>") executable = xsltproc.compile_stylesheet(stylesheet_file="test.xsl")
print(document)
output = executable.transform_to_string(xdm_node=document) print(output) except PySaxonApiError as err: print('Error during function call', err)
print('Example 2 \n') xml = """\ <out> <person>text1</person> <person>text2</person> <person>text3</person> </out>""" xp = proc.new_xpath_processor() node = proc.parse_xml(xml_text=xml) print('test 1\n node='+node.string_value) xp.set_context(xdm_item=node) item = xp.evaluate_single('//person[1]') if isinstance(item,saxonc.PyXdmNode): print(item.string_value)
section.p: Example 2: Python script using PyXsltExecutable (with SaxonC-HE):
section.samp:
from saxonche import *
with PySaxonProcessor(license=False) as proc:
print(proc.version) xsltproc = proc.new_xslt30_processor() executable = xsltproc.compile_stylesheet(stylesheet_file="test.xsl") executable.set_result_as_raw_value(True) executable.set_initial_match_selection(file_name="cat.xml") xdm_atomic_value = proc.make_integer_value(5) value1= proc.make_string_value("text")
executable.set_parameter("param",value1) executable.set_parameter("param2",xdm_atomic_value) result = executable.apply_templates_returning_string() print(result)
